Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jared Kim (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Helios SRE), Marco Ruiz (Helios VP Eng), Tara Singh (Helios Security)
Recording ID: ff-20260325-helios-01

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Quick follow-up to go over the postmortem doc we sent, confirm mitigations, and agree on runbook + acceptance criteria for the pilot of Redwood Dedicated.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: ok hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. we wanted to be respectful of time - 30 to 45 minutes - quick recap of the incident and then move into the mitigations and next steps.
[00:18] Dr. Lena Ortiz: thanks Maya. yes, appreciate you coordinating. we had a pretty rough week with the spike, so wanting to firm up the mitigations and timeline.
[00:32] Jared: hi all, Jared from Redwood infra. i'll go through the technical summary then we can dig into any traces you have. 
[00:45] Marco: quick note, Tara's on for security questions. we also have some exec interest so we'll try to keep the TL;DR up front.
[01:02] Jared: high level - on 2026-03-12 at ~02:14 UTC Helios saw a progressive increase in 95th/99th latency for the patient inference endpoint and then partial errors for about 18 minutes. Our analysis points to an interaction of two things: a KV cache invalidation during a deploy and an autoscaler threshold that was tuned toward conserving GPU capacity. the cache invalidation caused a burst of full-model requests and the autoscaler lagged, so botched sustained queuing on the serving nodes.
[01:45] Dr. Lena Ortiz: i remember the queue numbers; we were seeing a lot of cold starts. some of our traces showed repeated KV miss patterns.
[01:58] Jared: right - and a subtle one: the KV cache keys included a rolling prefix that we changed in a prior release; the rollout triggered a transient mismatch so the cache hit rate dropped from ~92% to ~18% momentarily. that multiplied request load to the GPU pool.
[02:25] Maya: to be extra clear, this wasn't an algorithmic model failure - the model stayed healthy, it was capacity/backpressure.
[02:40] Marco: ok, so cause = cache invalidation + autoscaler conservatism. why didn't our fallbacks kick in?
[02:50] Jared: two things - first, the fallback policy was set to roll to a smaller model variant but that variant wasn't compatible with the current KV prefix format. second, there was an error path in the routing logic that retried rather than failing fast, which extended the window where the serving nodes hit saturation.
[03:12] Tara Singh: from security perspective we need assurances about data residency and logs for audit. Can you confirm the logs are preserved?
[03:22] Maya: yes - we preserved all audit logs and request traces, we've shared redacted traces with your team and uploaded the full package to the secure link in the postmortem doc (https://redwood.ai/postmortem/helios-2026-03-12).
[03:40] Dr. Lena Ortiz: we saw the artifacts, thanks. i want to make sure the mitigation isn't just band-aid. what are the durable fixes?
[03:50] Jared: durable fixes we proposed in the doc: 1) pin the KV cache key schema in prod and add schema compatibility checks in the rollout pipeline; 2) relocate critical endpoints to a dedicated GPU pool for Helios (dedicated capacity) to avoid noisy neighbor impacts; 3) change autoscaler to proactive scaling (predictive) with smoothing window and warm-up buffers; 4) add an automated fast-fail path to avoid retry storms.
[04:28] Marco: can you quantify cost of dedicated pool vs host? our finance team will ask.
[04:36] Maya: we included a rough delta in the pricing appendix. short answer - dedicated increases base costs but reduces tail latency and outage risk; for Helios' 24/7 patient inference the unit economics often justify it. i can share the line-item estimate after this call.
[04:58] Dr. Lena Ortiz: for accept criteria, we'll need to run a benchmark that reproduces our typical burst profile and validate 99th is under the target and no error spikes.
[05:12] Jared: agreed. action plan is to run a synthetic load that mirrors your traffic shape (prefix cold misses, then steady). we'll schedule that with your SREs.
[05:26] Marco: about the KV key schema - is that something we have to change on our side?
[05:32] Jared: minor changes - we'll provide a compatibility shim and a validation script you can integrate into CI. it basically checks prefix and timestamp formatting.
[05:42] Tara Singh: and from compliance, we need to know KMS/HSM usage when moving to dedicated - who manages keys?
[05:50] Maya: for Redwood Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS; keys can be in your KMS account, Redwood will use external wrapping for disk encryption. we'll send the architecture note.
[06:05] Dr. Lena Ortiz: during the incident the autoscaler metrics had a gap. can you explain that?
[06:12] Jared: that's a telemetry gap we found - a config race during the deploy disabled the telemetry exporter for ~3m. we've instrumented a watchdog and an alert to prevent that.
[06:25] Marco: ok. what are the short-term mitigations you already applied?
[06:30] Jared: short-term we did: 1) temporarily increased autoscaler sensitivity and warm capacity to stop the immediate tail; 2) deployed a compatibility shim to restore KV hits for the rolling prefix; 3) added a temporary routing rule to fail fast on incompatible variants. these were applied within 40 minutes of detection.
[06:56] Dr. Lena Ortiz: i noticed the KV shim improved hit rate but we still had some error retries - will fail-fast remove those?
[07:05] Jared: yes, fail-fast plus shutting down the problematic route reduces retries; but long term we want dedicated pools + the cache schema guard.
[07:18] Marco: SLOs - can we get an SLA for the dedicated pool?
[07:22] Maya: yes, Dedicated comes with SLA options. we'll pull the SLA terms for Helios and mark outliers by region.
[07:32] Tara Singh: can you summarize what you'll need from Helios to proceed with dedicated pilot?
[07:38] Jared: a short list - sample tokenized traces (redacted is okay), an agreed traffic window to run bench, and a contact to approve temporary key access for the dedicated infra test.
[07:52] Dr. Lena Ortiz: i can own the traces and bench window. Marco will ok budget. Tara will confirm key governance.
[08:00] Maya: perfect. now on instrumentation - we propose adding continuous KV hit-rate monitors, end-to-end p95/p99 synthetic checks, and an alert that trips before autoscaler latency breaches.
[08:16] Marco: what's the threshold you'd recommend for that alert?
[08:19] Jared: we'd recommend a rolling 5-minute KV hit-rate drop below 70% OR a surge where concurrent requests increase >2x baseline and the autoscaler has not added nodes in 60s. both are configurable.
[08:40] Dr. Lena Ortiz: will these metrics be visible in our console or do you push them to our Datadog?
[08:45] Maya: both - Redwood Console will show per-route metrics and we can push a subset to your Datadog account. we'll share the mapping.
[08:56] Jared: also note we've folded in a change to routing logic so retries are capped and use exponential backoff - this reduces retry storms.
[09:08] Tara Singh: about audit logs - how long will you retain raw request traces? we need at least 90 days for PCI/HIPAA sensitivity.
[09:18] Maya: default retention is 30 days, but for enterprise we can extend to 90 or longer as an add-on. we'll include retention pricing.
[09:30] Marco: any risk to PII in logs during bench?
[09:34] Jared: we'll sanitize and tokenize before transferring. we can run the bench in your VPC if preferred so raw traces never leave your control.
[09:44] Dr. Lena Ortiz: excellent. i want to confirm rollback / canary process - if we roll a change that affects KV schema how do we avoid this again?
[09:53] Jared: two parts - build-time validators to flag schema changes, and a staged rollout that exercises a small percent of traffic with auto-rollback if KV hit rate drops over a threshold.
[10:10] Marco: how much engineering effort for the shim and validators on your side?
[10:15] Jared: the shim is done, validators are low effort - about 2-3 engineering days to integrate into your CI and another 2 days to run the canary automation. Redwood will staff the work.
[10:29] Maya: we'll attach the SOW estimate to the postmortem doc.
[10:33] Dr. Lena Ortiz: timeline then - when can we start the pilot?
[10:36] Maya: if we get traces by Mon 2026-03-30, we can schedule the pilot for week of 2026-04-06. runbook walkthrough prior to that week.
[10:47] Marco: sounds reasonable. finance will need the cost delta.
[10:50] Maya: i will email line-item pricing today and include options (dedicated baseline, burst buffer, autoscaler SLA).
[10:59] Jared: another ask - we'd like to run a controlled failure test to validate failover. propose a 10-15m simulated eviction to ensure the warm buffer handles the load.
[11:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: we want to see no patient-impact during that test. can we gate it to a staging-like traffic mirroring, and then final test in prod off-hours?
[11:22] Jared: yes, start in staging with your mirrored traffic, then we can coordinate a low-traffic production window.
[11:33] Tara Singh: security paperwork - we need updated SOC2 artifact references and any penetration test reports you have.
[11:40] Maya: we included SOC2 Type II and recent pen test summaries in the compliance folder. i'll re-share the direct links and confirm the latest dates.
[11:52] Dr. Lena Ortiz: ok good. a few small questions from the team about rollback of the shim - if the shim has performance impact, can it be toggled?
[11:59] Jared: yes, it's feature-flagged; toggling is immediate at the router layer. performance impact is negligible; it's mostly a key normalization step.
[12:10] Marco: do we need to change client SDKs?
[12:13] Jared: no, unless you want to adopt the schema guard in CI. the shim handles backwards compatibility.
[12:20] Maya: let's move to recap and next steps.
[12:24] Maya: recap - Redwood to share updated postmortem doc with action items and SOW (Maya) by 2026-03-27; Jared to schedule runbook walkthrough and set up bench test (Jared) by 2026-03-31; Helios (Dr. Lena) to provide tokenized traces and pick bench window (Dr. Lena) by 2026-04-02. Redwood to provide pricing appendix and SLA terms today.
[12:52] Marco: fine. any other open risks?
[12:55] Tara Singh: just ensure key governance during the pilot - we'll confirm scope of key access.
[13:02] Maya: noted - will include KMS flow diagram.
[13:06] Dr. Lena Ortiz: thank you, feel better about the plan.
[13:09] Maya: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email and post the doc.
[13:15] Jared: thanks all.
[13:18] Meeting end.
